basis.quote: How the True Physick, which is covered bark and rind, is to be got out, and rightly prepared by Fire
basis.why: The head of a whole chapter presents a course of operations (got out, prepared by Fire) leading to one result, the True Physick.

basis.quote: That it is to be fetcht out, and prepared truly, by fire.
basis.why: The author's own list of his heads announces the same course of operations for 'that Phisick'.

basis.quote: this Separatory art which teacheth rightly to discerne and seperate the Good from the Bad, the Profitable from the Unprofitable
basis.why: Names the operation of that course: separating.

basis.quote: The Chymicall way of Subtiliating Extracting, and Separating
basis.why: The text itself calls it a 'way' and names three operations in a row.

basis.quote: that pure and Christiline matter may be administred to our bodies
basis.why: Names the end the operations lead to: a pure matter given to the body.

basis.quote: the greatest miracle of Nature wrought by Art
basis.why: The chief Medicine of CH6 is presented as made by Art, not only praised.

basis.quote: the Moyst way of the Ancients not as yet intensly exalted to the eye of the Basilisk
basis.why: A named way and a degree of exalting: a course of operations toward the chief Medicine (covered; its steps are not given in these lines).

basis.quote: the fat or blood of the Sun and the Dew of the Lunary, be joyned into one body by the circular wheel of the Elements with the help of Art and Nature
basis.why: QUOTED: True Phylosophers ('religously affirming'): none attains 'the desired end' before this joining is done, with the help of Art. A course toward one end in covered words, in the chapter of the chief Medicine; the same paragraph says they swore never to write it plainly.

basis.quote: Gold animated by the Salt of Niture is made the chief subject of the Phylosophers metallick Physicks
basis.why: Names a matter and an operation on it (animated, made the chief subject). Interpreted as the work of the chief Medicine: the note stands in its chapter, beside the Phylosophers' freedom to 'give Names at their pleasure' (CH6.21), and speaks of 'metallick Physicks' in the plural; it does not itself name the one chief Medicine (note-only).

basis.quote: in this Rode or Kings Highway and Phylosophical Reason is to be accomplished
basis.why: The work is presented as a road along which something is accomplished. The words stand as what the many seekers 'have been perswaded'; whose words they are the line does not show (UNCLEAR in the marking list).

units.name: the True Physick
units.kind: Physick, got out and prepared by Fire

marked_at.quote: CHAP. I. Of the True Physick.
What that Phisick is which cureth mens diseases, and few Phisitians know it.
How the True Physick, which is covered bark and rind, is to be got out, and rightly prepared by Fire

parts.quote: Whereunto is added a perfect Philosophicall Description of the little World Man, almost forgotten and unknown.
parts.why: The author's list adds this Description to the first head on 'that Phisick': by his own marking it belongs to that head.

parts.quote: the Generation, Dignity, & Excelency OF THE MICROCOSM, Or Little World MAN
parts.why: The title of the Description that OPEN.24 adds to the first head; it describes man and presents no course of operations of its own.

parts.quote: CHAP. II. Where that True Physick is to be Found.
parts.why: Where its matter is found: the preparation that serves the process.

parts.quote: Where that True Phisick lyeth hid, and may be found.
parts.why: The author's announcement of the same head.

parts.quote: those three Families of Nature, the Vegetable, Animall, and Minerall
parts.why: The three kinds of matter it is found in.

parts.quote: this true Analysis and vitall Anatomy of bodies
parts.why: The operation on the matter, named in the chapter of getting it out.

parts.quote: to find out one out of those Three Families of Nature, that out of the same things in which all Physick is founded, viz. Animalls, Vegetables, and Mineralls
parts.why: The author's wish that each man skilled in Chymistry be set to search one of the three Families, to 'fetch out the most choyse Physicall Mysteries' by 'separating them by Fire': the course of U1 in U1's own words (three Families, fetch out, Fire), though the line stands in CH6. It speaks of 'all Physick' and of Mysteries in the plural, not of the one chief Medicine.

parts.quote: Reasons why the Spagyrick Physick duely prepared is to be preferd before other Hetroclite mixtures in the shops.
parts.why: The result of the process, 'duely prepared', set against shop mixtures; the note heads the reasons that begin at CH3.17, in U1's chapter (note-only).

parts.quote: this Divine Spagyrie, the most wonderfull and approved Art
parts.why: The Art that carries out the process.

parts.quote: There are four Pillars of Physick, Phylosophy, Alchymistry, Astronomy, and the Physicall vertue or medicine.
parts.why: The four Pillars that hold this Physick up, Alchymistry among them; the note stands where the author blames men who 'regard not the due preparation of their Medicines' (CH3.43) (note-only).

parts.quote: How, and with what Vertue, Physick worketh upon Mans body and cureth his Diseases
parts.why: How the prepared Physick works: its use, which the author's list ties to 'that Phisick' (OPEN.27).

parts.quote: As there are Three from which all Physick proceedeth, Mercury, Sulphur, Salt; so likewise there are three sorts of diseases, Mercuriall, Sulphurean, Saline
parts.why: Matches the Physick to the diseases it cures.

parts.quote: What manner of Phisitian that Phisick doth require for its Minister.
parts.why: The worker the Physick requires; announced as serving 'that Phisick'.

parts.quote: Secondly, a Physitian must be a good SPAGIRUS
parts.why: The Minister must be able to carry out the preparation.

units.why_one: The author's list of heads (OPEN.24-28) and the chapter heads CH1-CH5 all speak of one 'True Physick' / 'that Phisick': what it is, where it is found, how it is got out and prepared by Fire, how it works, and its Minister. Each later head serves that one thing, and the Description of the little World Man is 'added' to the first of them (OPEN.24); the chief Medicine has a head of its own (OPEN.29, CH6.0).

units.name: that one onely chiefe Medicine of the most Ancient Phylosophers

marked_at.quote: Of that one onely chiefe Medicine of the most Ancient Phylosophers
Of the universall and chiefe Medicine or Phisick of the most Ancient Philosophers
except only that universall and most famous Medicine which the most ancient wise Philosophers had from the beginning of the world

parts.quote: I shall here supply what yet pertaineth to that chief and universal Phylosophical Phisick
parts.why: Opens the chapter that treats it.

parts.quote: the fat or blood of the Sun and the Dew of the Lunary, be joyned into one body by the circular wheel of the Elements with the help of Art and Nature
parts.why: QUOTED: True Phylosophers: what must be joined, and by what, before 'the desired end' is attained; covered words, their plain meaning not given in these lines.

parts.quote: Gold animated by the Salt of Niture is made the chief subject of the Phylosophers metallick Physicks
parts.why: Interpreted: its chief subject and the operation that makes it so. The note says 'metallick Physicks', in the plural, and stands beside the Phylosophers' freedom to 'give Names at their pleasure'; that these are the one chief Medicine rests on the chapter it stands in (note-only).

parts.quote: the various and manifold metamorphosis of the Inferior Astronomy made in the cold
parts.why: Interpreted: the changes it works, in the cold, on what CH6.1 calls 'the Plannets of inferior Astronomy', whose drosse it makes vanish; the author reports them as seen. An effect of the Medicine, not a step of its making.

parts.quote: the Moyst way of the Ancients not as yet intensly exalted to the eye of the Basilisk
parts.why: The named way of its work and a stage of exalting.

parts.quote: in this Rode or Kings Highway and Phylosophical Reason is to be accomplished
parts.why: The road along which the work is accomplished; given as what the seekers 'have been perswaded' (voice UNCLEAR).

parts.quote: The originall of the Philosophicall Magistery.
parts.why: Magistery is a name CH6.49 gives this Medicine, and CH6.44 speaks of 'what is hid in the magistery of this Art'. Several defensible readings of 'originall': the first way of holding it, the 'Hapocraticall silence' the note stands beside, against which 'Most doe otherwise now'; or its source, God moving the Artist to a true Understanding, as the paragraph has from Lullius (note-only).

parts.quote: this choycest and admirable Magisterie
parts.why: Another of the book's names for it.

parts.quote: All diseases proceeding from the corruption of humors, how great and desperate soever their cures be, are healed by this universall medicine
parts.why: Its final result: it heals all such diseases.

parts.quote: And in this case the universall and chiefest medicine is of no effect, because no industry or skill of Artist or Nature can perpetuate the wedlock of life and death
parts.why: The limit of its effect, named in CH5.

parts.quote: study to finde out the Celestiall Stone in the last place
parts.why: Several defensible readings. (a) The Stone is this Medicine, and men study to find it last, after seeking the Kingdome of God; N283 calls the work 'this Stone'. (b) The Stone stands with the Kingdome of God as what men seek 'in the last place', that is too late, which is why none of the thousands finds the doors of Nature unlockt; N261 beside it names recourse to God as the one way to all Secrets. The lines given do not show that this Stone is the same thing as the Medicine.

parts.quote: that Ancient, True, & Philosophical Medicin
parts.why: Interpreted: the closing names it 'not yet fully known'; the words match the head's 'most Ancient Phylosophers'.

units.why_one: The author's list gives it a head of its own after the heads on 'that Phisick' (OPEN.29) and its own chapter (CH6.0). At the start he sets it apart from what he offers: nothing is more choice than 'these chief secrets of the more hidden Medicines here offered', 'except only' this one (OPEN.6). Its result differs from the True Physick's: one Medicine that heals all diseases of the humours (CH6.42), where the True Physick answers three sorts of diseases with their own medicines (CH4.10). A different final result makes it a different process.

left.quote: two of the most excellent Spagyrik Mysteries
left.why: The author sets two Mysteries before the reader; the lines given do not show which two they are, so the marking ties them to no unit of their own.

left.quote: these chief secrets of the more hidden Medicines here offered
left.why: What the author says he offers: few and choice Medicines, from which the same sentence excepts U2. The lines given do not show these Medicines one by one, nor whether they are the two Mysteries of OPEN.3. Interpreted: they fall under U1, since CH6.76 speaks of Medicins 'which must be prepar'd and try'd by Fire', the words of U1's head; no unit of their own from these lines.

left.quote: There is a two-fold Alchymy. Naturall, much esteemed by Artist. Sophisticall, as much detested by them.
left.why: A division of the Art: the Naturall serves U1 (N185 makes Alchymistry a pillar of Physick); the Sophisticall is reported to be rejected.

left.quote: their forged Cachochymicall and Sophisticall Arts, which have not so much as a spark of truth in them
left.why: Reported in order to reject it.

left.quote: There are also false and lying Theophrasteans prophaning by their avarice and timerity that Divine Physick
left.why: Rejected workers of the Physick, not a thing the book delivers.

left.quote: Thus also there is a fourfold Medicine
left.why: A division of medicine after the four Elements, inside the head of the True Physick; no course of operations of its own.

left.quote: Of this sort are the Fift Essences, Magisteryes, and the like.
left.why: Kinds named under the True Physick's head; no head or course of their own.

left.quote: to learn the preparations of those high Magisteryes and Elixirs
left.why: Several defensible readings: the higher preparations of U1 (in its chapter), or the work of U2 (CH6.49 calls U2 a Magisterie). Either way it has no head of its own.

left.quote: This fourth kind of Naturall Magick called Gamahaea doth all things invisibly and spiritually, by the help of Art
left.why: A kind of Magick named inside the Microcosm description; the author defers its fuller treatment ('a larger narration', MICRO.44).

left.quote: This part of Magick is called Gabalisticall, and is supported with three Pillars.
left.why: Its three Pillars (prayers, faith, imagination) are supports, not a course of operations to one result.

left.quote: Concerning Characteristicalll Cure which affecteth Naturall operations by words pronounced, written, carved and hanged about the neck
left.why: A kind of cure named within CH2; the marking gives it no head of its own.

left.quote: For in these Three principall Poynts also consisteth the whole Foundation of the Magicall and Cabalisticall Art
left.why: QUOTED: Paracelsus; three points of a foundation, not a course of operations the author delivers.

left.quote: For Faith, Hope and Love, follow knowledge, Adhaesion or cleaving to followeth Love, Union follows Adhaesion, in Union is Blessednesse and Wisdome.
left.why: A sequence of states of the soul, not operations of Art; a step of the Microcosm description.

left.quote: By meditating or contemplating we know, by knowing we are delighted, by delighting we adhere, by adhearing we possesse, by possessing we injoy the Truth
left.why: A sequence ending in enjoying the Truth, set in the head on the Physitian's duty; a note, with no head of its own (note-only). The note goes on to send the reader to other writers ('Read Div. Dionys.'), so it does not show the sequence to be the author's own words.

left.quote: A Physitian is compleated by 3 things
left.why: What completes the Minister of U1 (OPEN.28); qualities, not a course leading to a product.

left.quote: in three respects
left.why: QUOTED: Wimpeneus; respects in an argument inside CH5.

left.quote: There are four sorts of Tartar, springing from the fourfold fruits of the Elements by which we are nourished.
left.why: A discourse entered by the way ('since we are here fallen upon Tartar', CH5.32); it names a cause of disease, not a thing delivered.

left.quote: sometimes the sick person is not recovered by the best and fittest medicines that can be applyed, and that for these eight causes
left.why: A numbered list of why cures fail, within the head on the Physitian's duty.

left.quote: as we saw some years since in that famous Anwalding Panacaea
left.why: An instance the author saw, given as an example; no course of operations is marked for it.

left.quote: The MIND therefore of Adept Phylosophers
left.why: Speaks of the Adept who has U2, not of a further thing delivered.

left.quote: by this monument here left it may hereafter appear that that Divine Benificence hath not been denyed to men of our age also
left.why: Names the author's writing as a monument, not one thing set apart within it.

left.quote: I have inserted in their proper places in this Prolix and Admonitory Preface
left.why: The author's own account of what the Preface holds: what he gained by his labours, as far as may 'illustrate Physick and Phylosophy'. It sets no single thing apart; 'their proper places' points back to the heads, which the two units follow.

left.quote: this harvest of Chymicall Corn, and the First fruits of my increase, and this Spagyrick present of my difficult and laborious diligence
left.why: Names the author's whole offering, left 'to my Country and Common-wealth'; it sets nothing apart within it.

left.quote: Some thing in defence of the published Truth, as an Epilogue or Conclusion.
left.why: A head that only divides the argument.

changes.what: MICRO.0 (the Description of the little World Man): from left into U1's parts
changes.quote: Whereunto is added a perfect Philosophicall Description of the little World Man, almost forgotten and unknown.
changes.why: The author's list adds it to the first head on 'that Phisick'; the proposal's own reason said so and still left it outside. Like the heads on use and Minister, it belongs to U1 without presenting operations.

changes.what: CH6.30 (the three Families): from U2's parts into U1's parts
changes.quote: they might fetch out the most choyse Physicall Mysteries
changes.why: The line is a wish that men search the three Families and fetch out Mysteries, in the plural, by Fire; it does not say the chief Medicine's matter is chosen from them.

changes.quote: there doth not lye hid any more choyce and efficacious, then these chief secrets of the more hidden Medicines here offered
changes.why: The claim 'drawn from the same three Families (CH6.30)' is taken out, as that line does not carry it; added what 'except only' excepts U2 from: the Medicines here offered.

changes.what: left: OPEN.6, the Medicines here offered
changes.quote: these chief secrets of the more hidden Medicines here offered
changes.why: A marking of what the author offers that the proposal passed over; the lines given show no single Medicine, so it makes no unit.

changes.what: left: CH6.76, what the Preface holds
changes.quote: I have inserted in their proper places in this Prolix and Admonitory Preface
changes.why: The author's own statement of what this Preface carries, passed over by the proposal; it sets nothing apart beyond the heads.

changes.what: left: CH6.76, this harvest of Chymicall Corn
changes.quote: than which I suppose I could not leave behind me a better to my Country and Common-wealth
changes.why: The proposal called it an offering 'to the Prince'; the line leaves it to his Country and Common-wealth, the Prince being named there as the patron who bore the expences.

changes.what: U2 part CH6.18, the Celestiall Stone
changes.quote: when men seek the Kingdome of God, and study to finde out the Celestiall Stone in the last place
changes.why: The line bears two readings of 'in the last place'; the proposal gave one as if settled. Both are now stated.

changes.what: process basis and U2 part CH6.48, the Kings Highway
changes.quote: yet have been perswaded that they should never attaine the same, either by other means or any Arts
changes.why: The road is given as what the seekers are persuaded of, not plainly in the author's own voice; the marking list has it UNCLEAR. Said beside the line.

changes.what: U2 part CH6.38, metamorphosis of the Inferior Astronomy
changes.quote: the Plannets of inferior Astronomy, whose imperfection and drosse it causeth to vanish
changes.why: CH6.1 names inferior Astronomy as what the Medicine acts upon; the changes of CH6.38 are then its effect, seen by the author, not a step 'in its work'.

changes.quote: The Chymicall way of Subtiliating Extracting, and Separating
changes.why: The answer yes is kept; this line names the course as a way of three operations in the book's own words.

changes.what: process basis and U2 part: CH6.21
changes.quote: the fat or blood of the Sun and the Dew of the Lunary, be joyned into one body by the circular wheel of the Elements with the help of Art and Nature
changes.why: The paragraph of note N263, now given, holds a course toward 'the desired end' in covered words, given to the Phylosophers: the firmest line for a process of U2.

changes.what: process basis and U2 part N263
changes.quote: On this the hinge of the whole busines turneth
changes.why: Checked against the note: it names Gold animated as chief subject of 'metallick Physicks', in the plural, beside the Phylosophers' naming at pleasure; that this is the chief Medicine is now marked Interpreted.

changes.quote: Most doe otherwise now, who make thir boast among others that they have the clear knowledge of it
changes.why: The note gives no origin plainly; it stands beside the first silence and sets present boasters against it. Both readings of 'originall' are stated; it stays with U2.

changes.quote: regard not the due preparation of their Medicines
changes.why: Both notes checked and kept under U1: each stands in its chapter beside lines on preparing Medicines. Tagged note-only; the fourth Pillar is a vertue, not an art, so 'arts' became 'Pillars'.
Checked and kept in left; the note sends the reader on to other writers, so the sequence is not shown to be the author's own words.

open.point: U1's course is named only in general (got out, separated, prepared by Fire); the author's list words the head as a claim ('That it is to be fetcht out'). The lines given show no steps. Proposal's yes kept.

U2 is excepted from the Medicines here offered and reported as seen and tasted at another man's house; its making stands in the lines given only in covered words given to the Phylosophers, who swore never to write it plainly. Kept as a unit, wrought by Art.
Which two Spagyrik Mysteries are set before the reader, and whether they are units of their own; the lines given do not show them.
Whether 'the Phylosophers metallick Physicks' of the note is the one chief Medicine; the note does not say. Kept under U2 as Interpreted.
Whether the Celestiall Stone is U2.
Whether 'that Ancient, True, & Philosophical Medicin' is U2 or the True Physick of U1 ('True'; restored to the honor of Spagyrick Phisitians). Kept under U2.
Whether 'those high Magisteryes and Elixirs' belong to U1 or U2.
Whether the Kings Highway of CH6.48 is the same as 'the Kings high-way' the marking list has at CH6.35, whose paragraph is not given.
